question: Unlike vascular claudication, neurogenic claudication (spinal canal stenosis) is typically relieved by sitting or forward flexion of the spine, and the pedal pulses remain palpable.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true, and the distinction is clinically critical. Neurogenic claudication: relieved by sitting/flexion, worse with extension; normal pulses; often bilateral; canal stenosis on MRI. Vascular claudication: relieved by rest alone (not posture); reduced/absent pedal pulses; reproducible walking distance; ABPI <0.9.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In neurogenic claudication from lumbar canal stenosis, forward flexion widens the spinal canal and relieves symptoms — patients often describe being able to walk further when leaning on a shopping trolley ('shopping-cart sign'). Pedal pulses are normal because the arterial supply is intact. In vascular claudication, pulses are diminished and rest (not posture) relieves pain.
